chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah ibn 'A'yan from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man from the people of Basrah, a Shaybani named 'Abd al-Malik ibn Harmalah, passed by Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) asked him, 'Do you have a sister?' He replied, 'Yes.' He said, 'Marry her to me.' He replied, 'Yes.' The man left, and a companion of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) followed him until he reached his house. He asked about him, and it was said to him, 'So-and-so son of so-and-so,' and he was the master of his people. Then he returned to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'O Abu al-Hasan, I asked about this brother-in-law of yours, the Shaybani, and they claimed that he is the master of his people.' Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I will explain to you, O so-and-so, what I see and what I hear. Have you not known that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, elevated the lowly through Islam, perfected the deficient through it, and honored the blame-worthy through it? So there is no blame on the Muslim; indeed, the blame is the blame of the Time of Ignorance.'

key_terms.اللُّؤْم: Lowliness, baseness, or blame-worthiness, often referring to pre-Islamic social status.
key_terms.النَّاقِصَةَ: The deficient ones, those lacking in status or perfection.
key_terms.الْجَاهِلِيَّة: The Time of Ignorance, the pre-Islamic era characterized by tribal arrogance and lack of divine guidance.
key_terms.الْخَسِيسَةَ: The lowly or humble ones, those of low status.
key_terms.سَيِّدُ قَوْمِهِ: Master of his people, indicating nobility, leadership, or high status within the tribe.
key_terms.شَيْبَانِيٌّ: A member of the Shayban tribe, often used to denote a specific lineage or characteristic in Basra.
key_terms.صِهْر: Brother-in-law or son-in-law, referring to the marital relationship.

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq mean by 'the blame is the blame of the Time of Ignorance'?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) seeks to marry the sister of a Basran man, 'Abd al-Malik ibn Harmalah, prompting a companion to verify his social standing. Upon learning the man is considered a 'master of his people' (likely referring to tribal nobility or wealth), the Imam clarifies that Islam has superseded pre-Islamic hierarchies by elevating the humble and honoring the worthy. He asserts that the 'lowliness' (lu'm) of the Jahiliyyah no longer applies to Muslims, establishing that true nobility is derived from faith rather than lineage or status.
